title: UK zero-rates VAT on domestic electricity (effective 01 October 2026) — a dated, government-quantified -0.10pp cut to CPI
source: EST: gov.uk/government/news/new-pm-cuts-tax-on-household-electricity-bills-to-give-breathing-space-on-cost-of-living, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — published 21 July 2026, announcing Prime Minister Andy Burnham's cut of VAT on domestic electricity from 5% to 0% effective 1 October, worth 'around GBP 45 off the yearly Ofgem price cap in October' and 'estimated to reduce CPI inflation by around 0.10 percentage points and RPI by around 0.14 percentage points'. Corroborated from a second, independent primary: Ofgem's 26 August 2026 press release announcing the October-December cap (ofgem.gov.uk/press-release/energy-price-cap-will-rise-4-october-2026) states 'The Government's decision to remove VAT from all domestic electricity bills is reflected in this update' and that 'the VAT reduction means electricity bills will remain broadly stable' while gas bills rise 8%. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a UK government or regulator announcement. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2026-09-16, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-cpi-2026-09-16 LANE, 2026-09-09. This is a POLICY EFFECTIVE DATE, not a print: it is here because it is the rarest thing a macro calendar gets — a mechanical, pre-announced, government-quantified move in a national CPI series, with the size (-0.10pp) stated by the issuer before the fact. It first appears in the OCTOBER 2026 CPI print, published 18 November 2026, which is AFTER the 05 November MPC meeting — so the MPC must forecast it rather than observe it, and it is a live argument against the strip that priced a 94.6% chance of a higher Bank Rate by 2026-12-17 (centralbank.watch, 09-08). Two caveats kept on the record: it is stated as TEMPORARY, running to the end of the 2026-27 financial year (31 March 2027) with extension to be considered at the 28 October Budget, so the same -0.10pp reverses in April 2027 unless renewed; and it excludes Northern Ireland, which stays on EU VAT rules, so the CPI effect is a GB-weighted one. It also does NOT offset the same cap period's 8% gas rise. Tiered LOW: symbols: [], no rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only.
